t: LeetCode 3196 – Maximize Total Cost of Alternating Subarrays
o: Split nums into contiguous subarrays to maximize the sum of alternating-sign costs; each subarray starts with a positive sign. In [1,-2,3,4], cutting before the 4 gives (1+2+3) + 4 = 10. The only decision per element is whether it continues the current subarray (sign flips) or starts a new one (sign resets to +). This is a textbook DP over positions with a sign-state dimension. n up to 10^5 demands O(n).
k: State: best cost for a prefix where the last element carries a + or − sign.
Starting a new subarray always enters the '+' state; continuing flips the state.

a.n: Approach 1: Bottom-up DP with two states
a.i: Let f[i] = best cost of prefix ending at i with nums[i] positive-signed, g[i] with negative-signed. Continuing alternation: g[i] = f[i-1] - nums[i]. Either continuing or cutting: f[i] = max(f[i-1], g[i-1]) + nums[i]. Answer is max(f[n-1], g[n-1]).
s: For each subsequent x: newG = f - x; newF = max(f, g) + x.
Return max(f, g) at the end.
a.t: O(n) — one constant-time transition per element

a.i: The same recurrence written recursively: best(i, pos) = maximum total cost for the suffix starting at i, where pos indicates whether nums[i] takes a + or − sign. Memoize on (i, pos); cutting to a new subarray corresponds to transitioning to best(i+1, true) from either state.
s: Define dfs(i, pos): if i == n return 0.

If pos: return max(nums[i] + dfs(i+1,true) [continue], nums[i] + dfs(i+1,false) [flip]) — but a fresh start is captured by allowing the '+' state from anywhere; simplest: from '+' you may flip or restart '+'; from '−' you may only restart '+'.
a.t: O(n) — each of the 2n memo states computed once
a.sp: O(n) for the memo table (plus recursion stack)

w: Present the iterative two-state DP first — it is the cleanest and uses O(1) space. Pitfalls: forgetting that a new subarray must start with '+', initializing g to -infinity (not 0), and 64-bit sums (values up to 10^9 · 10^5). Edge cases: single element (answer nums[0]), all-negative arrays (every element its own subarray). Follow-up: minimize instead of maximize, or limit the number of cuts (add a third DP dimension).
